result.title: Game2Real-Bench: Do Toy Games Reveal and Transfer to Real-World Visual Reasoning?
result.summary: Visual reasoning is an important capability for vision-language models (VLMs) to understand visual evidence, spatial structure, constraints, and state changes. Existing evaluations mainly rely on real-world data or procedurally generated tasks. Real-world data preserve natural complexity, while procedural games provide controllable generation and verifiable solutions. However, it remains unclear whether abilities measured in toy games correspond to real-world visual reasoning and whether game examples can support transfer. We introduce Game2Real-Bench, a benchmark that studies these connections across four capability groups, including fine-grained perception, spatial reasoning, constraint reasoning, and sequential planning. We construct 1,000 procedurally generated game samples with executable verification and curate 400 real-world samples aligned by shared reasoning requirements rather than visual similarity. We evaluate 25 representative VLMs and observe strong game-to-real consistency, with Pearson and Spearman correlations of 0.935. We further study one-shot game-to-real transfer on four models. Constraint reasoning improves for several models, while fine-grained perception declines with game demonstrations. We also construct Game2Real-Dataset with nearly 24K verified game samples across 18 tasks and 65 QA families. Our benchmark, dataset, and code are available at https://github.com/QingAnLiu/Game2Real-Bench.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Game2Real-Bench，构造 1000 个可执行验证的程序生成游戏样本与 400 个按共享推理需求对齐的真实世界样本，评测 25 个 VLM 在细粒度感知、空间推理、约束推理与序列规划上的表现，并研究单样本游戏到真实的迁移。
AI.relevance_reason: 作为 VLM 视觉推理的诊断性基准，其「游戏—真实」高相关以及迁移中约束推理提升、细粒度感知下降的现象，可供核查视觉证据筛选与任务必要信息在真实场景中的保留与使用情况。
